title: Medicaid Hours Wallet for Gig Workers
one_liner: A phone-based monthly proof-of-work ledger that turns gig, cash and self-employment activity into state-accepted documentation and 30-day cure packets, paid for by the Medicaid plans and health centers that lose revenue when members drop.
customer: Medicaid managed care organizations with expansion-adult lines, and FQHC and community health center networks. Medicaid is 43-50% of health center revenue, and an MCO is paid capitation per member-month. End users are expansion adults aged 19-64 with irregular income. The MCO or health center pays per retained member; the enrollee pays nothing.
problem: CMS's interim final rule (June 3, 2026) requires states to implement 80 hours a month of work or activity, or $580 a month in income, by Jan 1, 2027. Compliance is checked at application and at renewal, and a noncompliance notice gives 30 calendar days to cure. CBO projects about 4.8M coverage losses from work requirements, largely from reporting complexity. About 9 in 10 affected patients are expected to qualify for an exemption or already comply, yet many will still lose coverage on documentation. Nebraska went live May 1, 2026 with self-attestation, but about 28,000 people there must document twice a year and the state plans to move to verification.
solution: An enrollee-side SMS and app tool. It ingests bank and payment-app statements, gig platform earnings exports (Uber, DoorDash, Cash App, Venmo), pay stub photos and logged volunteer or class hours. It computes whether each month clears $580 or 80 hours and generates the state-specific verification packet. It sends look-back-month reminders and prepares the 30-day cure response. It flags likely exemption candidates, such as medically frail members, from plan claims data. The plan or clinic dashboard shows at-risk members and cure success. The tool only assists and never determines compliance, which is what federal rules allow plans to do.
why_now: The interim final rule was published June 3, 2026, and the national start date is Jan 1, 2027. Nebraska's live rollout is the preview of what other states will face when verification replaces self-attestation. CMS is encouraging automation, but states are spending on caseworker portals, notices and screening tools, not on income documentation for gig workers.
revenue_model: $3-8 per at-risk member per month billed to the MCO, or a success fee of $50-150 per member retained through renewal. FQHC SaaS at $2-5k per month per site with an outcomes dashboard. Later, state contracts for a self-employed and gig documentation module.
non_obvious_insight: Vendors such as Salesforce are building state-facing portals for applicants and caseworkers. The parties with a P&L at stake, the MCOs and health centers, are not yet being sold a member-side tool. KFF's roundup of state outreach plans covers notices, websites and screening tools but does not describe how self-employed or irregular income will be documented (https://www.kff.org/medicaid/medicaid-work-requirements-federal-outreach-requirements-and-state-plans/). State wage-data matching misses 1099, cash and gig work by design. Georgetown's CCF warns that 'verification in this context means burdensome documentation requirements for enrollees' (https://ccf.georgetown.edu/2026/05/11/the-new-medicaid-work-reporting-requirements-are-here-dont-let-the-nebraska-soft-start-fool-you/). The retention math is lopsided: a plan or clinic can pay a few dollars a month per member to protect several hundred dollars of monthly revenue. Sources: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/03/2026-11094/medicaid-program-community-engagement-requirement-for-certain-individuals and https://www.pointcare.com/blog/how-to-prevent-medicaid-coverage-gaps-in-2026
first_30_days: Build the Nebraska flow first, since it is already live. Recruit 50 gig and self-employed Medicaid enrollees through one FQHC partner. Measure how many can produce a compliant $580 or 80-hour packet within 30 days. Take those results to two MCO member-engagement and quality leads for a paid pilot. Sign an LOI with one health center network before Jan 1, 2027.
